text:
maria: Heads up — onboarding a community LLaMA variant and seeing a mismatch between tokenizer.json and tokenizer_config.json. Fast tokenizer load succeeds but special tokens are missing at inference-time.
kevin: hmm that usually means fast tokenizer (tokenizers lib) picks up tokenizer.json only and our loader expects tokenizer_config.json for 'added_tokens' or chat template mapping.
sam: can you paste the two files? sometimes HF conversions produce a tokenizer.json that contains specials under different keys.
maria: here are the relevant bits — pasted from repo: ```
# tokenizer_config.json
{
  "do_lower_case": false,
  "unk_token": "<unk>",
  "pad_token": "<pad>",
  "eos_token": "</s>"
}
``` ```
# tokenizer.json (truncated)
{
  "model": { ... },
  "added_tokens": [{"id":50256,"special":true,"content":"<|system|>"}],
  "tokenizer_class": "BPE"
}
```
maria: fast loader uses tokenizer.json -> sees added_tokens fine. but our redwood conversion path reads tokenizer_config.json first for chat template specials and then falls back incorrectly, so when runtime serializes tokenizer metadata for the quantized model, the specials get dropped.
kevin: ah the bug: conversion step merges tokenizer_config into runtime metadata using a shallow merge, and tokenizer.json keys like `added_tokens` are ignored. shallow merge overwrites instead of deep merging.
julie: we hit this earlier in a bring-up — it caused small but measurable quality regression on prompts with system messages. the eval suite flagged ~2% drop on instruction-following.
sam: quick repro: convert the HF archive with our script and inspect model_metadata.json produced by redwood-convert. command: `./tools/redwood-convert --source hf --input model_dir --out out/`
kevin: sample diff from the convert run: ```
- "special_tokens": ["<|system|>"]
+ "special_tokens": []
```
kevin: root cause is config priority ordering: we used `tokenizer_config.json` > `tokenizer.json` but didn't merge array fields.
maria: workaround for now: copy `added_tokens` entries manually into tokenizer_config.json under `special_tokens` and re-run convert — works for the current QA run.
julie: can we add a unit test to conversion that checks parity between token sources? like verify that union(added_tokens, special_tokens, pad/unk/eos) across both files is preserved.
kevin: yes, I'll add a test and change merge to deep-merge arrays by identity on `content` or `token` field. also add a warning if tokenizer.json exists but tokenizer_config.json is missing expected fields.
sam: also flag for oncall: if runtime sees missing specials at load time, raise a structured error instead of silently proceeding — that would have prevented the eval regression slipping through.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline note: new redwood-convert unit tests added to PR #3142 will run in CI.
maria: thanks — I'll backfill the failing evals once test PR lands. also filing a small patch to our HF conversion docs to recommend including added_tokens in tokenizer_config.json for private model owners.
kevin: opened fix PR with tests. cc @maria @sam for review. :thumbsup:
julie: great — rolling patch to staging after CI green.
maria: leaving a note in the model onboarding checklist: check both tokenizer files and run `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json').get_special_tokens_map())"` to inspect.
kevin: we should also add a small conversion flag `--prefer-fast` to copy over fast-only fields when present.
sam: agreed. stopping the bleeding for now.
